item.title: Noir-CKB update: what I decided after the direction check, what you can try today, and where this is going (1 posts)
item.description: About a month ago I shared a direction check here for noir-ckb, asking for feedback on what I was building. I got really thoughtful replies, mostly around two questions: Where should a proof live in a CKB transaction (Lock or Type?), and is Noir → Groth16 even the right backend, given its per-circuit trusted setup. This post is the follow-up: what I decided, what exists now that you can actually run (including on testnet), and the longer-term picture of where I want this to go. It’s a long one, sorry in advance Quick recap, if you’re new to this noir-ckb lets you write a rule in Noir, prove it off-chain, and have a CKB script verify the proof. item.title: Tactus O1: First Based EVM Rollup on CKB (1 posts)
item.description: A follow-up on Tactus O1. The latest experiments exposed two problems I need to address. Generating a ZK proof took roughly 78 minutes on my laptop, while verification on CKB consumed about 3.985 billion cycles, exceeding mainnet’s 3.5 billion limit. The prototype works on a devnet with a higher limit, but is not mainnet-ready. The prover also replays execution history from genesis, so the cost grows as the chain gets longer. The other concern is settlement lag. CKB can keep accepting EVM transaction batches while their proofs are still pending. That means transaction ordering can move ahead of verified settlement, potentially delaying withdrawals indefinitely if proving cannot keep up....

item.title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes (1 posts)
item.description: Hi @Ayoub_Lesfer, Happy to support this. I created a test campaign on the current version and the app is nice to use. It worked smoothly and I didn’t hit any bugs. The concept is a very good fit for the CKB cell model: a campaign is a cell, each pledge is its own cell, and the lock only allows two exits. Nobody holds the money in between, and anyone can check the rules on-chain. Making it a product on testnet first and coming back for the audit and mainnet once there’s usage is the right order. item.description: cover1920×1080 137 KB A follow-up to the introduction on Scryve, with the technical side: what each floor does on chain, how the game is built, how the town works, and how to join its first wave. item.title: 分享一个 Tinder 版预测市场应用的想法 (1 posts)
item.description: 关于初始流动性，不知道可不可以类比早年的微博问答模式，粉丝花费100元向大V提问题，大V回答后赚到100，之后有人如果对这个问题感兴趣需要付费查看，然后最开始提出问题的粉丝就可以从中赚钱了。回到这个长尾/利基预测市场平台，提交预测题干就相当于提问题，也可以类比成发射meme币，需要提供比如100刀流动性，后续只要参与的人多起来Ta就能从中盈利，这样也能激励所提预测的质量。
